title: Measure whether mutations can be generated, because that is the whole economic claim
description:
T6 from the exploration drawer, and the FIRST thing to do. Frank's call 2026-10-30: 'T6 is fine.'

THE CLAIM UNDER TEST. The design says mutations are cheap to generate AND mechanically verifiable, and that this is what cracks the triangle: per item the cost becomes one generation plus N environment runs with no human judgment in the loop. SLICE 1'S THREE PATCHES WERE HAND-WRITTEN, so the claim is an argument rather than a result.

WHY IT GOES FIRST. A negative result changes the design's SHAPE, not its scale. If mutations cannot be generated, the authoring unit is four hand-made things per item and Orbis is a hand-built corpus with a better grader, which is the corner the triangle says you cannot escape by effort. Finding that out after authoring six items by hand is finding it out late.

THE MEASUREMENT, and it has a verdict so it is safe unattended. Point a model at the seat-desk app and ask for N mutations as patches. Then run the EXISTING gate over each one and count:
  - how many apply at all
  - how many the reference CATCHES
  - how many the reference is SILENT on, meaning the break is unobservable
  - how many produce a per-test vector that DUPLICATES another, meaning two breaks teach the same thing
  - how many are breaks nobody would ever write

THE LAST COUNT IS THE ONE WITH NO ORACLE and it is the honest limit. The design drawer already says so: 'Generatable is not the same as worth generating', and a break nobody would make is a contrived exercise wearing a verdict. Report that count as a JUDGMENT and say it is one. Do not convert it to a score.

THE FIRST FOUR ARE ALL MECHANICAL and the gate already computes them. That is the point: the measurement needs no new instrument.

WHAT A PASS LOOKS LIKE, described rather than numbered per D4. Enough of the generated mutations are caught and mutually distinguishable that an author would rather filter a generated set than write three by hand. If most are silent or duplicate, the generator is producing noise and the filter costs more than authoring.

RED: run the gate over a generated mutation set and get a per-mutation table of applies, catches, vector, and whether the vector duplicates another.
Files: src/orbis/, items/playwright/01-seat-desk/

title: Write two or three lessons, show Frank, and let his reaction become the exemplar set
description:
D1 as Frank settled it on 2026-10-30: 'Yes, but what we do is just do a limited number of lessons to start with, and I give feedback.'

THIS IS THE ONE PIECE THAT CANNOT BE DONE UNATTENDED AT SCALE, and the reason is measured rather than cautious. An LLM judging prose register scores kappa near 0 against human annotators and 0.08 span precision. Three of the five dimensions that predict a human slop judgment have no automatic measure, and TONE is one of them. Frank's complaint was that the default voice is 'grating and hard to read', which is a Tone complaint. So a critique-and-revise loop with a model critic revises against NOISE.

WHAT THE RESEARCH SAYS WOULD WORK. Specify the register POSITIVELY with exemplars. Negated instructions are a documented weak spot, and exact-count constraints score 0 percent so a density cap cannot go in a prompt and must be a post-generation gate. Readability indices and word counts are the WRONG gate: Verbosity, Gunning-Fog and Repetition were NOT significant predictors.

SO THE SHAPE IS: write TWO OR THREE lessons, not a corpus. Show them. His reaction is the exemplar set, and with exemplars in hand the next batch can be generated against them with a post-generation gate on the dimensions that do have a measure. Do not generate ten lessons and ask him to review them, which converts his feedback from a design input into a chore.

WHAT A LESSON IS NOT. It is not the worked answer, which is the page's spoiler reveal. It is the teaching prose that precedes an item.

D6 ALSO REQUIRES CHARTS, DIAGRAMS OR TABLES WHERE THEY EARN THEIR PLACE. Mayer's multimedia principles apply and so do their expert boundary conditions, which matter because Frank is not a novice. One caution with a measurement behind it: EXPERTISE REVERSAL DOES NOT LICENSE LESS COHERENT PROSE. Skilled high-knowledge readers benefit from HIGH cohesion, and splitting a sentence usually drops the connective, which turns a stated relation into a required inference.

A STANDING CONSTRAINT ON ALL OF IT: prose a human reads goes through the frank-writing skill. Never an em dash, never a semicolon, American spelling.

STOP AFTER THE BATCH. Do not start the next one without his reaction. This bead is finished when he has read two or three lessons and said something about them.

title: The page: a task, a per-line spoiler reveal, and the click recorded as a side effect of reading
description:
D8, and it follows from the pedagogy rather than from a presentation preference. Frank: 'more flexibility unless there's a strong reason otherwise.'

WHAT THE PAGE IS FOR. Per-line spoiler protection cannot be done on paper, and a page can RECORD THAT THE CLICK HAPPENED. That click is the commitment step the design needs, for a measured reason: the benefit of a reveal is the attempt that preceded it rather than its accuracy. Kornell, Hays and Bjork 2009 found guessing before seeing the answer beat seeing cue and answer together, with only 4 to 5 percent of guesses correct.

THE FAILURE TO AVOID, and it is measured in the predecessor. THREE capture surfaces there were specified and left EMPTY, every one of them a surface that asked the learner to record something. The drill runner only got past it by recording as a SIDE EFFECT of asking for the next item. So the reveal must record by being used, and must never ask Frank to log anything.

WHAT IT RENDERS. The task statement, the reveal of the worked answer line by line, and a margin note per line saying roughly which part of the solution it is, so he knows what he is about to uncover without the margin being an answer. That margin design is Frank's and it is the best part of the original sketch.

PLAIN PYTHON EMITTING HTML. mkdocs is NOT installed on this box, which is why the predecessor carries a --skip-docs flag and why its scripts/server cannot run here. Choosing mkdocs imports that friction on day one. Chiron's markdown-to-PDF step via pandoc and weasyprint becomes markdown-to-HTML, which is simpler rather than harder.

D6 SAYS LESSONS MUST CARRY CHARTS, DIAGRAMS OR TABLES, so the renderer needs a path for them. SVG or Mermaid may remove the need for Chiron's PlantUML-to-PNG step and its 23-line repair prompt. Decide that when the first lesson needs a diagram, not before.

OUT OF SCOPE HERE: the lesson prose itself, which is its own child, and any progress reporting beyond recording the reveal.

RED: open the page for an item, reveal two lines of the worked answer, and find both reveals recorded without having been asked to record anything.
Files: web/, src/orbis/

Lines revealed in an earlier sitting render already open. RED is a Playwright test of the page itself under tests/.

title: Author four to seven more Playwright items in slice 1's shape
description:
D2 from the 2026-10-30 conversation. Frank on the count: 'I think that works' to a description rather than a number, which is D4 applied to this bead. Read it as four to seven, and stop when the shape is clearly holding rather than when a counter hits a target.

WHY MORE THAN ONE. One item cannot tell a general instrument from a fitted one. The runner, the four cells and the gate were all built against the seat desk, and anything they assumed about it is invisible until a second item disagrees.

THE RECIPE IS IN .claude/rules/orbis-practice.md and it is six steps in a fixed order. The step that is most often skipped and least optional: every item ships at least three candidates the gate must REJECT, one vacuous, one silent-everywhere, one uncollectable. The silent-everywhere one is the whole point, because a pass-or-fail instrument calls it correct.

SUBJECT COVERAGE, as coverage and never as a per-item target. V2-PLAN's rule from the predecessor applies verbatim: coverage is an end-of-run AUDIT, never the problem-list generator, because organizing by construct produces items whose purpose is to exercise a construct, which is contrived by construction. Author off-ramp and audit afterwards.
Shapes worth having between them, as an audit list: waiting and auto-retry, a form with validation, navigation and history, a dialog, network interception or a stubbed response, something with a list that reorders, and something where the obvious selector is the wrong one.

ITEMS ARE WHOLE TASKS FINISHABLE IN ABOUT TEN MINUTES. That floor is measured: below it the correlation with the real skill goes to zero. Single-line exercises showed NO correlation with code writing where multi-line ones correlated highly.

EACH ITEM IS INDEPENDENT, so this is parallelizable across workers one item each, with disjoint directories. The gate is what makes that safe.

RED: scripts/test passes with every new item, and for each one a mutation made to stop applying is named by tier 1.
Files: items/playwright/
notes:
SETTLE THE CONVENTIONS BEFORE AUTHORING ANY ITEM, or author one and throw it away. Measured in tla-puzzles 2026-11-04, drawer_tla_puzzles_findings_e5283b17bf0961a3eb662b78.

ITEM 01 OF A FAMILY IS THE WORST PROMPT AND THE LONGEST, measured over 64 items against a full audit's verdicts:

  index   underdetermined   avg words
  01          6 of 8           270
  02          5 of 8           232
  08          1 of 8           222

NOT A FATIGUE EFFECT. The two authoring waves of 32 read 50.0% and 40.6%, three items apart, and both waves covered all eight indices so position and wave are cleanly separated. So this is NOT 'the generator gets tired', it is 'the first item is written before the pattern exists'.

THE MECHANISM, with direct evidence. A family's conventions get established BY writing its items. The table of what should be possible, the published count, the foreclosing row: each is a convention the first item could not follow because it had not been invented yet. sequences/05 resolves the identical phrase ambiguity that sequences/01 fumbles, and 05's table SHOWS the resolution while 01's does not. Same author, same family, later item, better.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS BEAD. Slice 1's seat-desk item IS Orbis's item 01, written before any convention existed, and the measurement above says it is the one most likely to be wrong in a way the gate cannot see. So:

  - Before authoring item 02, write down what an Orbis item's conventions ARE: what the task statement must state, what the candidate set must contain, how the mutations relate to the reference's tests. .claude/rules/orbis-practice.md is the start of that and it was written FROM slice 1, which is the right direction.
  - Then RE-READ the seat desk against those conventions rather than assuming it set them correctly.
  - Expect to change it. An item that defined the pattern by accident is not the same as an item that follows it.

AND THE SECOND HALF, which is the one with a number attached. BLOAT PREDICTS BREAKAGE: underdetermined prompts averaged 251 words and 1.6 questions against 218 and 1.1 for determined ones, fifteen percent longer and forty-five percent more questions. Four of the five longest prompts were in the worst family.

So a generated task statement that runs long or asks several questions is SUSPECT, and that is cheap to check. Treat it as a suspicion and never as a defect: the longest prompt in that corpus, 514 words, was determined.

title: The Playwright runtime works end to end, so Frank can sit down and use it
description:
THE GOAL, in Frank's framing on 2026-10-30: he opens a page, works a Playwright item, self-checks, reveals the worked answer per line, and the system knows whether he was right. One subject, hand-fed. No generator.

Against that, slice 1 has the VERDICT and nothing else. Missing: more items, the page with the reveal, a progress store, and a few lessons.

D9 is why this is the epic rather than the generator. Chiron built a real generator and died in the runtime plumbing, and the runtime is both the half that killed the last attempt and the half that proves anyone will use it.

WHAT MAKES UNATTENDED WORK SAFE HERE, and it is the one property to protect. Every item gets gated: the reference passes the real app, fails every mutation, and no two mutations produce the same per-test vector. An item that does not discriminate cannot ship. scripts/test runs selfcheck on every item, which grades the reference AND every candidate the item carries to be rejected.

WHAT IS NOT SAFE UNATTENDED, and it is scoped rather than deferred. Lesson prose. An LLM scores kappa near 0 against human annotators on register and 0.08 span precision, so a model critic revises against noise. Frank's ruling: a LIMITED number of lessons to start, and he gives feedback. See the lessons child.

ORDER, agreed with Frank 2026-10-30: the mutation-generation measurement FIRST, because it is the whole economic claim and a negative result changes the design's shape rather than its scale. Then items and the page, which are independent. The store after. Lessons whenever he has bandwidth to react.

title: A progress store: what has been attempted, what was revealed, what is next
description:
The runtime needs to remember across sittings, and nothing does yet.

WHAT IT HOLDS. Per item: attempted or not, the verdict the gate gave, which answer lines were revealed, and when. The reveal log is the interesting half, because it is the commitment record the spoiler design rests on and it is written as a side effect rather than asked for.

WHAT IT MUST NOT BECOME. A mastery score derived from a model's claim about anything. That is Chiron's exact failure, recorded in bd memory chiron-died-of-plumbing-not-pedagogy: its assessment prompt told the model to encourage regardless of correctness and evaluate_response was a passthrough, so its numbers ran off the model's opinion of its own dialogue. The gate's verdict is a fact about a run and is the only thing worth storing as one.

KEEP IT SMALL AND BORING. SQLite or a JSON file. This is plumbing, and plumbing is what killed the predecessor at 4,561 lines against 490 of prompt, so the budget here is deliberately tight. If it grows past a file and a few functions, something has gone wrong.

LOWER PRIORITY THAN THE PAGE ON PURPOSE. The page can record to a file it owns, and the store can be factored out of that once there is something to factor. Building the store first invents a schema for data nothing produces.

Files: src/orbis/
design: progress.py holds two append-only JSONL logs under run/: reveals (moved out of page.py) and attempts. 'gate attempt <item> <file>' grades a learner file with G1+G2 (G3 is about the reference) and appends {item, candidate, accepted, cells per environment, at}. The page shows the last attempt per item and the command. Nothing derived, no score: the gate verdict is the only fact stored.
